title: A Study in Scarlet
logline: When an injured army doctor meets an eccentric scientific detective, their new partnership is tested by a baffling double murder whose solution exposes a decades-old love, persecution, and revenge.

elements.text: A hansom rolls through London traffic.
You mustn’t blame me if you don’t get on with him.
It seems to me, Stamford, that you have some reason for washing your hands of the matter.
Holmes is a little too scientific for my tastes—it approaches to cold-bloodedness.
A young man springs up with a test-tube in his hand.
I’ve found it! I’ve found it.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide exterior of a hansom rolling through London traffic, the carriage crossing the frame from left to right.
Locked-off corridor two-shot of Stamford and Watson walking together and speaking about Holmes, with the dissecting rooms receding behind them.
Locked-off medium shot of Holmes springing up with a test-tube in his hand and declaring his discovery.

elements.text: Stamford brings Watson into the chemical laboratory. Holmes works among glass retorts and chemicals, scarcely looking up.
I think we may consider the thing as settled—that is, if the rooms are agreeable to you.
Watson looks back toward the hospital. Stamford continues toward the crossing.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame of the chemical laboratory as Stamford brings Watson in; Holmes works among glass retorts and chemicals, scarcely looking up.
Locked-off over-the-shoulder frame from behind Watson as Holmes confirms the arrangement.
Locked-off frame holding Watson looking back toward the hospital while Stamford continues toward the crossing.

elements.text: Holmes eats toast at the breakfast table. Watson reads a marked article.
I listen to their story, they listen to my comments, and then I pocket my fee.
The commissionaire enters and hands Holmes the blue envelope.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame of the breakfast table in 221B Baker Street at night: Holmes eats toast while Watson reads a marked article.
Locked-off medium close-up of Holmes as he describes his usual consulting work.
Locked-off medium two-shot at the entrance as the commissionaire enters and hands Holmes the blue envelope.

elements.text: Holmes studies the departing commissionaire through the window. A great blue anchor marks the back of the man's hand.
Wonderful!
Commonplace.
My dear fellow, what does it matter to me.
But he begs you to help him.

Yes. He knows that I am his superior, and acknowledges it to me; but he would cut his tongue out before he would own it to any third person. However, we may as well go and have a look. I shall work it out on my own hook.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium-wide interior view from the sitting-room side of the window; Holmes studies the departing commissionaire outside, with the blue anchor on the man's hand visible through the glass.
Locked-off two-shot across the table, Watson's admiration answered by Holmes's dry dismissal.
Locked-off medium close two-shot of Holmes and Watson beside the table as Holmes weighs the request and finally agrees to investigate.

elements.text: Holmes leaves the hansom a hundred yards from Number 3.
He studies the wet grass beside the path. Twice he stops. A smile touches his face.
The attendants lift Drebber. A wedding ring strikes the floor and rolls beneath the stairs.
There’s been a woman here. It’s a woman’s wedding-ring.
This complicates matters.
You’re sure it doesn’t simplify them?
Holmes writes down the constable’s address. He does not look at the word on the wall.
Rache, revenge.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide exterior frame of the path and Number 3. Holmes leaves the hansom in the distance, studies the wet grass, stops twice, and smiles within the held composition.
Locked-off low frame beneath the stairs. The attendants lift Drebber, the wedding ring strikes the floor and rolls beneath the stairs, and the investigators debate what it means.
Locked-off medium close-up of Holmes writing down the constable’s address, deliberately keeping his attention on the page as he explains the German meaning of Rache.

elements.text: Rance sits forward on the horsehair sofa. Sleep still weighs on his face.
Rance looks from Holmes to Watson. The half-sovereign glints between Holmes’s fingers.
What sort of a man was he?
He was an uncommon drunk sort o’ man.
His face—his dress—didn’t you notice them?
He was a long chap, with a red face, the lower part muffled round——.
That will do.
Holmes turns for the door. Rance remains seated, unconvinced and uneasy.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium shot of Rance sitting forward on the horsehair sofa, sleep weighing on his face.
Rack focus from Rance looking between Holmes and Watson to the half-sovereign glinting between Holmes's fingers, then holding the questioning exchange in the same setup.
Locked-off wide shot holding Holmes as he turns for the door while Rance remains seated, unconvinced and uneasy.

elements.text: The sitting-room is quiet. Watson waits beside the half-open door.
The Lord be thanked! Sally will be a glad woman this night. That’s the ring.
Here is your ring, Mrs. Sawyer. It clearly belongs to your daughter, and I am glad to be able to restore it to the rightful owner.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame of the quiet sitting-room, with Watson waiting beside the half-open door.
Locked-off medium close-up holding Mrs. Sawyer's relieved face as she identifies the ring.
Locked-off medium two-shot as Watson presents the false ring and speaks with courteous certainty.

elements.text: Gregson sits in the arm-chair, puffing complacently at his cigar.
Well done! Really, Gregson, you are getting along. We shall make something of you yet.
Gregson’s smile fades. His glass remains halfway to his mouth.
Stangerson too! The plot thickens.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium-wide frame from axis side A, holding Gregson in the arm-chair as he puffs complacently at his cigar.
Locked-off medium close-up from axis side A on Holmes as he answers Gregson with dry approval.
Slow dolly in from axis side A toward Gregson as his smile fades and his raised glass stalls, while Holmes registers the new information.

slug.location_name: Halliday’s Private Hotel, Little George Street
slug.text: INT. HALLIDAY’S PRIVATE HOTEL, LITTLE GEORGE STREET - DAY

elements.text: Holmes takes the small pill-box from Lestrade. Two pearly-grey pills rest inside.
Now, Doctor, are those ordinary pills?
From their lightness and transparency, I should imagine that they are soluble in water.
Precisely so.
He cuts the second pill. Dissolves it. Adds milk.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium close-up on Holmes receiving the small pill-box from Lestrade; the two pearly-grey pills remain clearly visible inside.
Locked-off medium two-shot of Holmes and Watson as Holmes questions him, Watson examines the pill's qualities, and Holmes confirms the deduction.
Locked-off close-up of Holmes cutting the second pill, dissolving it, and adding milk; the prepared dose fills the foreground.

elements.text: Wiggins appears at the door, cap in hand.
Just ask him to step up, Wiggins.
Hope roars and wrenches free. He hurls himself through the window.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium-wide frame of the Baker Street sitting room, with Wiggins appearing at the door, cap in hand.
Locked-off medium close-up of Holmes addressing Wiggins and directing him to bring the cabman forward.
Handheld medium-wide frame as Hope roars, wrenches free, and drives toward the window.

elements.text:
The Inspector writes at a crowded desk.
Hope sits opposite, wrists joined before him.
Are you a Doctor?
Yes; I am.
Then put your hand here.

The Inspector stops writing.
Watson keeps his hand on Hope’s chest.
Do you consider, Doctor, that there is immediate danger?
Most certainly there is.
You are at liberty, sir, to give your account, which I again warn you will be taken down.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium-wide frame of the crowded police-station chamber: the Police Inspector writes at the desk while Jefferson Hope sits opposite with his wrists joined before him.
Locked-off two-shot of Jefferson Hope and John Watson, holding their eyelines across the chamber as Hope asks Watson to place his hand on him.
Locked-off three-shot of the Police Inspector stopping his writing while Watson keeps his hand on Hope's chest; the Inspector questions Watson, then grants Hope permission to speak.

elements.text: A grey shawl lies beneath a boulder. The desert stretches empty in every direction.
A young man lifts Lucy. Two others take Ferrier by the arms.
You must come and see us. Now I must push along, or father won’t trust me with his business any more. Good-bye!

shots.setup: Wide locked-off frame beneath the boulder, the grey shawl in the foreground and the empty desert extending in every direction.
Medium locked-off frame as a young man lifts Lucy and two others take Ferrier by the arms.
Medium close-up locked-off frame on Lucy inviting Hope to visit before turning back to her business.

elements.text: The latch CLICKS. Ferrier reaches the door.
Ferrier rises. Young remains seated.
No; of course not. I shouldn.

shots.setup: locked-off wide frame of the Utah doorway; the latch clicks and Ferrier reaches the door
locked-off medium two-shot; Ferrier rises while Young remains seated
locked-off medium close-up of Lucy answering and describing the message that will be sent

elements.text: The side window opens by inches. One by one, they slip into the garden.
A narrow track climbs toward Eagle Cañon. Hope finds the waiting animals.
The Holy Four.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame from the garden, holding the farmhouse side window as it opens by inches and the fugitives slip into the garden.
Locked-off wide frame facing the narrow track as it climbs toward Eagle Cañon and Hope finds the waiting animals.
Locked-off close frame on Ferrier among the animals as he gives the password.

elements.text: Hope leads them through the defiles. The horses pick their way over rock.
Hope disappears into the ravines.
He drops the meat and runs.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame on the Utah mountain defiles. Hope leads the horses through the narrow rock passage as they pick their way across the foreground and recede into the depth of the landscape.
Locked-off wide frame on the ravines. Hope moves away from the camp and disappears into the winding rock passage.
Locked-off wide frame as Hope drops the meat in the foreground and runs deeper into the defile.

elements.text: The door bursts open.
A rifle cracks across the mountains. A bullet smashes into a wall beside Stangerson.
Town after town slips behind him. The ring remains in his pocket.

shots.setup: Wide locked-off interior frame facing the closed doorway as it bursts open into the room.
Long locked-off mountain frame as a rifle cracks across the landscape and the bullet smashes into the wall beside Stangerson.
Lateral locked-off composition through successive towns slipping behind Hope while the ring remains in his pocket.

elements.text: Hope’s hand closes around Lucy Ferrier’s marriage ring.
I knew of their guilt though, and I determined that I should be judge, jury, and executioner all rolled into one.
The ring disappears into his pocket.
At Euston, Drebber and Stangerson part. Hope stays with Drebber.
I could not catch what Stangerson.
Drebber runs to Hope’s cab and climbs inside.
Drive me to Halliday’s Private Hotel.

shots.setup: locked-off close-up on Hope’s hand closing around Lucy Ferrier’s marriage ring, then holding as the ring disappears into his pocket; Jefferson Hope’s confession continues over the image.
locked-off medium two-shot at Euston as Drebber and Stangerson part and Hope remains with Drebber; Hope’s confession continues over the held image.
locked-off medium view beside Hope’s cab as Drebber runs into frame, climbs inside, and orders Hope to drive him to Halliday’s Private Hotel.

elements.text: Hope unlocks the house and leads Drebber into the dark front room.
You dog! I have hunted you from Salt Lake City to St. Petersburg, and you have always escaped me.
What do you think of Lucy Ferrier now?
He chooses one and swallows it.

shots.setup: Wide locked-off frame from the room's left side of the action line, the opened front door admitting Hope and Drebber into the dark room; Hope leads Drebber across the frame from left to right.
Medium close-up from axis side A on Hope confronting Drebber, the matchlight carving his face as he invokes Lucy Ferrier.
Close-up from axis side A on Drebber choosing one pill and swallowing it.

slug.location_name: Halliday’s Private Hotel, Little George Street
slug.text: INT. HALLIDAY’S PRIVATE HOTEL, LITTLE GEORGE STREET - DAY

elements.text: Early morning. Hope reaches Stangerson’s room by ladder from the lane.
The hour has come when you must answer for the life you took so long before.
Stangerson does not reach for them. He springs from the bed.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame of the hotel room and the lane-side window as early morning light reveals Hope reaching Stangerson’s room by ladder.
Locked-off medium close-up on Hope as he addresses Stangerson across the bed, holding the accusation in a steady frame.
Handheld medium frame as Stangerson springs from the bed toward Hope, the framing breathing and correcting with the sudden attack.

elements.text: Hope’s cab waits at the curb.
At 221B, the door opens.
Hope steps inside. Holmes closes behind him.
Hope keeps his hands still.
I can tell my own secrets, but I don’t get other people into trouble.
Not a doubt of that.

shots.setup: Locked-off wide frame of 221B Baker Street in daylight, Hope’s cab waiting at the curb.
Locked-off medium-wide view of 221B as the door opens, Hope steps inside, and Holmes closes it behind him.
Locked-off two-shot of Jefferson Hope keeping his hands still while he answers Sherlock Holmes, with Holmes replying from the same side of the action line.

elements.text: The next evening. Holmes has spread a newspaper across the table.
Watson looks from the newspaper to Holmes.
The face supplied the fear. The smell supplied the poison. The ring supplied the woman. The telegram supplied Hope.

shots.setup: Locked-off medium-wide view of the study table as evening light rests across the room; Holmes spreads the newspaper across the table.
Rack focus begins on the newspaper and transfers to Watson as his eyes move from the page to Holmes.
Slow dolly in toward Holmes and the marked newspaper as he assembles the face, smell, ring, and telegram into his chain of evidence; the foreground markings slide subtly past the frame edges.

elements.text: Holmes hands Watson the newspaper.
Watson unfolds the Echo. His eyes move down the column. Lestrade and Gregson receive the credit for Jefferson Hope’s capture.
Never mind. I have all the facts in my journal, and the public shall know them.

shots.setup: Medium two-shot, locked-off camera. Holmes hands Watson the newspaper in the center of the frame.
Insert close-up, locked-off camera, Watson unfolds the Echo and reads down the column as the printed credit for Jefferson Hope’s capture remains visible.
Over-the-shoulder medium close-up from behind Holmes, locked-off camera, Watson speaks while the open journal rests before him.
